Title: 29 foreigners held as police raid luxury bungalow, hotel scam hubs
Article:
MELAKA TENGAH: Police have smashed two online scam syndicates operating out of a luxury bungalow and a hotel here, arresting 29 foreigners.
The syndicates, which targeted victims in Vietnam and China, were crippled in separate raids by Melaka Tengah police.
Melaka Tengah police chief Assistant Commissioner Halim Abas said the first raid on a two-storey bungalow in a resort area yesterday evening led to the arrest of 15 men aged between 21 and 40.
The suspects comprised 14 Vietnamese nationals and one Chinese national.
Initial investigations found that the premises was being used as a call centre for non-existent loan and love scams targeting victims in Vietnam.
Halim told a press conference that the syndicate had been operating since early October, with suspects posing as customer service officers to contact victims.
"Police seized 11 computer sets, 24 mobile phones, remote controls, translation devices and 15 passports, with the total seizure estimated at RM43,400.
"Each suspect was paid about RM2,500 to carry out the operations," Halim said.
In a separate raid on Tuesday afternoon, police arrested 14 Chinese nationals at a hotel in Melaka Raya.
Halim said the suspects, comprising 11 men and three women aged between 21 and 55, were using four hotel rooms as an operations centre for an online investment scam targeting victims in China.
He said the syndicate had been active since mid-September, paying each suspect about RM3,000 to act as a customer service representative.
Police seized 33 mobile phones, four laptops, a tablet, translation devices, 96 prepaid SIM cards and RM6,400 in cash, with the total seizure valued at RM47,500.
All 29 suspects are being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating and Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act for illegal entry.
The offences are punishable by jail terms, fines and caning.

Title: Son of Myanmar's Suu Kyi says had first call in five years
Article:
YANGON: The son of Myanmar's Aung San Suu Kyi said Thursday he was allowed to speak to the detained former democratic leader for the first time in more than five years.
"Today, I was finally able to speak with my mother, Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, after more than five years. Hearing her voice again means more than words can express," Kim Aris said in a post on Facebook.
Suu Kyi is under house arrest in the capital, Naypyidaw, according to Myanmar authorities, where she has been sequestered since being unseated in a 2021 military coup.
It was not immediately clear how Aris – who lives in the United Kingdom – spoke to his mother, who won the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to bring democracy to Myanmar.
However, he posted images accompanying his Facebook post which appeared to show him standing outside the Myanmar embassy in London.
"I am deeply grateful to everyone who has stood by my mother and me. I believe your voices helped make this moment possible," his Facebook post said.
"But my mother is 81 and remains unjustly detained. One conversation is not regular family access."

Title: Evidence, sovereignty issues pose hurdles to transboundary haze law
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia faces major challenges in enacting transboundary haze pollution laws, particularly in obtaining evidence and addressing sovereignty issues that could undermine its enforcement.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the proposed legislation required comprehensive scrutiny, given the jurisdictional challenges involved in enforcement and its potential implications for diplomatic relations with other countries.
"The merits of enacting such legislation have been examined from various angles to ensure it can be implemented and enforced effectively.
"The main challenge is obtaining sufficient evidence to establish the source of pollution and identify those responsible," he said at a media engagement here today.
Arthur said the evidence required included the location and coordinates of fire sites, land ownership, parties conducting activities in the affected areas and proof linking the fires to haze pollution.
However, such information was generally subject to the jurisdiction, confidentiality requirements and sovereignty of the countries concerned, making evidence gathering for enforcement purposes more difficult, he added.
He said any proposal to introduce new legislation must therefore be assessed comprehensively to ensure its provisions were practical and enforceable.
The assessment must also consider the implications for diplomatic relations with regional countries and ensure the proposed legal framework could effectively address transboundary haze pollution, he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia demands effective action from Indonesia on transboundary haze
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia will demand effective action from Indonesia to tackle fires causing transboundary haze when it raises the issue at the Asean Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Manila early next month.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said Malaysia respected its bilateral ties with Indonesia but had the right to demand measures to protect Malaysians' health and well-being.
"We respect our good relations with Indonesia, but we also have the right to demand effective action when transboundary pollution affects our people.
"Malaysia is ready to help. We hope Indonesia will step up efforts to put out fires at their source and take firm action against those responsible," he said at a media engagement on the haze situation here today.
Arthur said the cabinet had decided to raise the issue regionally, with the Foreign Ministry tasked with bringing it up under the Asean framework.
He said Asean members had to respect the principles of national sovereignty and decision-making by consensus, but Malaysia remained firm on its right to demand clean air for its people.
"The foreign minister will brief the government on the outcome of the meeting before further action was decided, he added.
He said Malaysia has also proposed science diplomacy and a sustainable haze fund through Asean mechanisms to strengthen regional prevention, preparedness and monitoring, while continuing to examine policy and legal measures to address transboundary pollution.
"Malaysia will also host the Sub-Regional Ministerial Steering Committee on Transboundary Haze Pollution meeting next year as part of ongoing efforts to strengthen regional cooperation in tackling the problem.
"We are trying out some methods to overcome the worsening haze situation and if proven to be effective, we will announce the measures next year," he said during a media editors engagement session held at the ministry today.
Arthur said the government had taken preventive measures before the haze situation worsened, including activating the National Open Burning Action Plan on Feb 15 and convening the National Haze and Dry Weather Main Committee meeting on June 15 to strengthen agencies' preparedness.
He also met his Indonesian counterpart in Bali on July 8, followed by an Asean ministerial meeting the next day.
Further diplomatic engagements and formal offers of assistance were made in August and September.
"Action had begun before the haze became increasingly serious. However, I acknowledge that the results have yet to meet the expectations of the people," he said.
The Interim Asean Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control raised its alert level to the highest stage on Aug 26.S
"Satellite observations on Oct 14 showed extensive clusters of hotspots in southern Sumatra and parts of Kalimantan, while monsoon winds carried smoke into Peninsular Malaysia, western Sarawak and Singapore" he added.
The ministry also has warned that El Niño is expected to persist until the middle of next year, with conditions forecast to intensify to a "Super El Niño" from October to January next year.

Title: Canada's Carney visits Turkiye in push to ease US trade dependence
Article:
ANKARA: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney will meet President Tayyip Erdogan in Turkiye on Thursday, in the first bilateral visit by a Canadian leader, as he seeks to expand trade ties and reduce reliance on the United States.
Carney and Erdogan are expected ‌to sign a declaration deepening cooperation in four areas including defence and energy, a person briefed on the matter said.
A Turkish diplomatic source said the bilateral ties will be upgraded to a "strategic partnership."
Carney is on a global trade blitz that he hopes will help buffer Canada from a trade war with the US, where President Donald Trump has applied sweeping tariffs and questioned the neighbouring country's sovereignty.
Carney's plane landed in the Turkish capital Ankara at 0800 GMT and he was set to meet Erdogan at the presidential palace around 1200 GMT.
Nato member Turkiye is seeking new investment and collaboration for its burgeoning defence industry, new nuclear power plants and mining sector.
Carney's office said the visit aims "to position Canada as a key partner in trade and investment."
He is expected to meet with prominent Turkish business leaders during the trip, the Turkish diplomatic source said.
Concrete potential steps that could be taken on trade, investments, defence industry, security and energy will be discussed during the trip, the Turkish source said.
Although trade between Canada and Turkiye is tiny – Turkiye accounted for less than 0.3 per cent of Canada's total merchandise trade or C$4.34 billion (US$3.09 billion) – bilateral trade has risen by nearly 50 per cent in the past five years.
"This trip is part of the geopolitical necessity of signaling to Americans that we are not sitting around waiting for them," said Bessma Momani, professor of political science at the University of Waterloo.
In the last year, Canada has signed more than 20 trade deals as part of Carney's push to double non-US exports in the next decade.
He flew to Beijing in January to reset fractured relations with China, striking a deal that slashed tariffs on electric vehicles and canola.
Despite criticism that China is a security risk, given Canadian authorities previously found China had interfered in at least two federal elections, Carney has described China as a "more predictable" trading partner than the US.
However, Canada still sends nearly 70 per cent of exports to the US.
Turkiye's crackdown on the opposition since 2024 and arrests targeting the LGBTQ+ community have drawn criticism. But Carney has focused less on rights than his predecessors.
"Carney will have to walk a very fine line in Turkey between opening new economic possibilities for Canada while trying to maintain Canada's middle power role in fighting for equality," said Anna Agathangelou, a professor of politics at York University.
Ankara says the judiciary is independent, denying that investigations or court cases are politically motivated.
At the Nato leaders' summit in July, Carney and Erdogan launched negotiations for a free-trade agreement, where Turkiye also agreed to join Canada's Defence, Security and Resilience Bank as a founding member.
Turkiye has held talks with Canadian engineering firm AtkinsRealis as well as South Korea's ​Korea Electric Power Corporation and China's State Power Investment Corporation about potentially building its planned second and third nuclear power plants.
In 2024, Canada removed weapons-export controls on Turkiye, including on optical ​technology used in drones that Turkiye exports to dozens of nations.
Canada mainly exports lentils, aircraft and electronics to Turkiye, and imports ​medical devices, fishing vessels, aircraft engines and jewelry.

Title: Zetrix AI yet to pay RM314mil in outstanding government revenue, says Loke
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd has yet to make any payment towards the RM314 million in outstanding government revenue, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said.
He said the suspension of the company's appointment as a Road Transport Department (RTD) collection agent had not disrupted summons payments or other services, which remained accessible through alternative channels, including MyJPJ.
"In terms of payment, they have yet to pay.
"Other services are still available through MyJPJ. There are other options," he said at a press conference after the launch of Phase Three of the Masjid Jamek LRT station upgrade project.

Title: China slams 'Cold War mentality' after new EU Arctic plan
Article:
BEIJING: China opposed on Thursday "using Cold War mentality" to stoke conflict over the Arctic, after the European Union linked Beijing's cooperation with Russia in the region to security concerns.
The EU unveiled on Tuesday a push to boost Arctic surveillance and expand icebreaker fleets, alluding to China's growing "strategic ambitions... as it deepens its partnership with Russia."
Europe, China, Russia and the United States are jostling for influence in the polar region that is seen as an important trade route.
This summer, a Chinese shipowner began a weekly container service through the Arctic on an express route to Europe, prompting concerns over vessels warming polar ice.
Beijing and Moscow agreed this week to "expand cooperation" in Arctic shipping, including increasing the number of routes between Russian and Chinese ports, according to a joint communique released after a meeting between their prime ministers.
Asked about the new EU strategy and calls from foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas to bolster the bloc's defences in the Arctic, China denounced what it called a "Cold War mentality."
"China's activities in the Arctic are aimed at promoting the Arctic's peaceful, stable and sustainable development, and are in accordance with international law," foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said during a regular news conference.
"Using Cold War mentality to create factions and incite geopolitical confrontation is not conducive to the peaceful and stable development of the Arctic region," she said, without naming the EU specifically.

Title: 'We are everywhere,' police warn Melaka election candidates, political parties
Article:
MELAKA: State police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar has warned election candidates, political parties and their supporters not to violate any law during the campaigning period.
"We are everywhere. We will watch your every move... we will see it and we will know (what you do).
"Besides CCTV (closed-circuit television) cameras, we have drones. So, you will not get away with anything. Be careful.
"Don't come begging for help after you've been detained," he said during a briefing on the 16th Melaka election at the state police headquarters.
He said police would ensure that security and public order are maintained throughout the election period.
Dzulkhairi reminded all parties to avoid provocations, threats, slander, and the 3R issues of race, religion and royalty, which could trigger tensions within society.
He said political differences should be handled maturely, while any disputes should be resolved through legitimate channels without resorting to emotionally-driven actions.
"What is important is to avoid raising 3R issues and spreading slander. These matters must be handled carefully to prevent public anxiety.
"Our focus is on maintaining public order and safety. Issues involving 3R and related matters will be referred to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission for investigation," he said.
He said the briefing was held to explain to political party representatives what they can and cannot do in the lead-up to and throughout the state election.
He said some 140 political party representatives from across Melaka, along with representatives from relevant agencies, attended the briefing.
In addition to police, representatives from MCMC and the Election Commission were also invited to provide explanations within their respective areas of jurisdiction.
Meanwhile, Dzulkhairi advised all parties to act responsibly when using social media, particularly by verifying the accuracy of information before sharing it, to prevent the spread of fake news and content that could trigger tensions.
He also urged all campaign activity organisers to pay attention to safety, the suitability of venues and traffic flow, and to consult the relevant authorities on related requirements.

Title: Norway's wealth fund posts US$30bil loss in Q3
Article:
OSLO: Norway's US$2.3 trillion sovereign wealth fund, the world's largest, reported on Thursday a loss of 278 billion Norwegian crowns (US$29.71 billion) for the third quarter, with a return of minus 0.5 per cent on its global investments.
"The fund's return was close to flat, ending slightly negative as rising interest rates led to weaker results on our fixed-income investments," deputy CEO Trond Grande said in a statement.
Investing the Norwegian state's revenues from oil and gas production, the fund owns on average 1.5 per cent of all listed companies globally, making it the world's largest single investor.
Overall, the fund is invested in some 7,100 companies as well as bonds, property and renewable energy projects.

Title: 'PN is back': Takiyuddin celebrates court reprieve ahead of Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: "PN is back!"
That was the jubilant declaration by Perikatan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan after the High Court today granted the coalition a stay on its suspension and deregistration by the Registrar of Societies (RoS).
The decision brought relief to the coalition just nine days before nomination day for the Melaka election, allowing it, according to its lawyers, to resume political activities and preparations to contest under its own name and symbol.
Speaking at a press conference after the proceedings, Takiyuddin expressed his gratitude to the coalition's legal team, led by former Dewan Rakyat speaker Tan Sri Azhar Azizan Harun.
He described the ruling as a significant development for PN, which had been fighting to overturn its suspension on Sept 23 and subsequent deregistration on Oct 20.
"I don't want to say too much. I just want to say two things. PN is back! PN is back!" he said.
Also present at the press conference were Wawasan Negara president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin, Gerakan president Datuk Dr Dominic Lau Hoe Chai, Malaysian Indian People's Party president P. Punithan, Pejuang president Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir, Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man and Datuk Seri Shahidan Kassim.
Lawyer Rafique Rashid Ali, who was part of the coalition's legal team, said the court's decision meant PN could resume its normal political activities, including contesting the Melaka election.
He confirmed that the stay covered both the suspension and deregistration orders issued by RoS.
"In simple terms, it means maintaining the status quo.
"We can contest, we can use the logo and we can continue all our activities, including in Melaka and later in Sarawak," he said.
However, Rafique stressed that the High Court had yet to determine whether RoS' decisions to suspend and deregister PN were lawful.
He said those questions would only be decided during the substantive hearing of the coalition's judicial review application.
Rafique said the dispute was not merely about the coalition's political survival but also involved the interests of voters and elected representatives.
Earlier, High Court judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad
allowed PN's stay application
pending the disposal of its judicial review application, finding exceptional circumstances warranting interim relief.
The judge ruled that RoS' decision to cancel PN's registration on Oct 20 did not automatically render the stay application academic.
However, the court did not determine the legality of RoS' decisions, leaving those issues to be decided during the substantive judicial review.

Title: Kerian Industrial City targets RM700mil in development value
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kerian Industrial City (KIC) is expected to create new opportunities for industrial growth, attract investment and support the expansion of local businesses.
Spanning 116.15 hectares with an estimated gross development value of RM700 million, KIC is expected to generate 12,000 jobs, according to Perak State Development Corp (PKNPk).
The development will create opportunities for investors, industrial operators, and support service providers to expand their operations in Kerian, accelerating the local economy and contributing to Perak's broader economic growth.
Located in northern Perak, Kerian has a strong industrial foundation, with the Parit Buntar Industrial Estate serving as one of the district's key drivers of manufacturing and supporting industrial activities.
PKNPk chief executive Datuk Redza Rafiq Abdul Razak said KIC presents significant opportunities for industry collaboration in recruiting engineers, technical personnel, and industrial trainees, as well as conducting applied research to meet the needs of the private sector.
"We want KIC's success to bring tangible benefits by creating job opportunities that enable Perak's young people to build their careers and secure a better future in their home state.
"Through strategic collaboration between industry players and educational institutions, we can realise this potential, in line with the aspirations of Perak Sejahtera 2030," he said.
KIC is part of Perak's broader economic development network, which also includes Automotive High Technology Valley, Lumut Maritime Industrial City, Silver Valley Technology Park and KIGIP.
Each development has its own distinct role and strengths, contributing to the state's overall economic capacity across the automotive, technology, maritime, manufacturing and green industries sectors.
Perak chief minister Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said KIC represents a strategic initiative to strengthen Kerian's economic capacity, expand investment opportunities, and ensure local communities benefit from industrial growth.
"It is time for Kerian to strengthen its economic potential and transition from an agriculture-based economy towards higher-value industries. Kerian must now prepare to enter a new era, building on its agricultural strengths while embracing higher-value industrial activities.
"KIC is more than just an industrial development. It is a catalyst for investment, creates economic opportunities, and ultimately brings greater prosperity to the people.
"This is in line with the aspirations of Perak Sejahtera 2030 to build a progressive, competitive, and prosperous state," he said.
Asia Bina Group managing director Datuk Yong Chai Seng said KIC's success should not be measured solely by its ability to attract investment, but also by the extent to which the development creates opportunities for local vendors, suppliers, contractors and businesses to participate in the industrial supply chain.
"Through close collaboration among all stakeholders, we want to ensure that local businesses have opportunities to expand their capacity and strengthen their capabilities, enabling the benefits of this development to continue reaching the local community over the long term," added Yong.

Title: Indonesia's fire hotspots fall, but wildfire threat remains
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia remains on high alert for wildfires despite a decline in hotspots over the past week, with the sporadic rainfall still not enough to put them out, a disaster agency official said on Thursday, as students on Borneo island staged protests against the government's handling of the crisis.
Indonesia has been battling its most intense forest fires in 11 years, with the El Niño weather phenomenon driving up temperatures and leaving the country's vast stretches of forest and peatland more vulnerable to fire.
The persistent fires have caused hundreds of thousands of cases of respiratory illness in Indonesia and badly affected air quality in neighbouring Singapore and Malaysia, with the transboundary haze drawing heavy criticism across the region.
According to data from the EU's Copernicus climate monitoring service, carbon dioxide emissions from Indonesian fires from Oct 15 to Oct 21 reached 14.44 million metric tons, down from 22.22 million tons over the preceding seven days.
The number of "high-confidence" hotspots stood at 565 on Thursday, according to Indonesian forest ministry monitoring platform Sipongi, down from over 1,200 on Oct 14.
"Based on the latest developments, the number of hotspots has shown a decline; however, the trend remains volatile and is not yet uniform across all regions," Berton Panjaitan, a spokesperson for Indonesia's disaster mitigation agency, told Reuters.
Indonesia has deployed more than 69,000 firefighting personnel, up from around 44,000 in mid-September, as well as around 50 aircraft to conduct waterbombing and weather modification operations. Authorities are also testing new methods to put out fires, including special chemicals and the use of dry ice for cloud seeding.
Indonesia's dry season started earlier than usual this year and has also lasted longer. The rainy seasonnormally starts in October, but the country's weather agency said it will be delayed until November.
"The potential for new hotspots to emerge persists, especially if rainfall remains uneven and the sources of the fires have not been fully addressed," Berton said.
At least 100 university students in Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan province staged a protest at the regional house of representatives to demand more concrete action to extinguish the fires, a local news channel showed.
Hundreds of students in Pontianak in West Kalimantan and Samarinda in South Kalimantan also held demonstrations on Wednesday to protest against the local government's handling of the fires, according to local media.
Berton said authorities would maintain firefighting efforts and strengthen patrols.
"The goal is to prevent new fires and ensure that fires that have been extinguished do not reignite," he added.--AFP

Title: GOF: Illegal entries not confined to Golok River
Article:
RANTAU PANJANG: Undocumented migrants are entering Malaysia through various routes, not just the Golok River, prompting the General Operations Force (GOF) to strengthen security along land and sea borders.
Internal Security and Public Order Department deputy director Datuk Mohamad Suzrin Mohamad Rodhi said this was based on briefings from brigade representatives yesterday.
"Anyone arrested for entering the country through illegal routes will face enforcement action, followed by the relevant legal proceedings," he told reporters during a visit to the border today.
Suzrin said the GOF worked with state police contingents, district police stations, the Marine Police and the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency to detect and respond to border incursions within their respective areas of responsibility.
He said intelligence sharing was crucial to ensuring enforcement teams could act regardless of the entry points used.
On the use of technology, including drones, to detect incursions, he said the force relied on various intelligence sources, with personnel stationed at control posts and interception teams ready to respond to detected offences.
"Once an incident is identified, information will be channelled to all relevant personnel in the border area to enable immediate action," he said.
Suzrin said intelligence indicated that smuggling tactics were constantly evolving, with operations believed to involve land-based smugglers and other parties facilitating the activities.
"Various methods are being used to carry out incursions, so we must constantly improve our preparedness and strengthen cooperation among enforcement agencies," he said.
He added that the GOF would continue coordinating operations with the Kelantan police contingent and other contingents responsible for border areas, in line with directives from the police leadership.
Meanwhile, four additional GOF posts will be set up along the Malaysia-Thailand border in Kelantan to strengthen surveillance and improve operational readiness.
Suzrin said 12 existing GOF posts were undergoing upgrading works, while the four new posts were planned according to logistical requirements and expected to begin construction next year.
He said he had been briefed on efforts to upgrade and relocate posts along the Golok River, including moving them to higher ground to improve operational coordination and border surveillance.
The relocation was necessary as records showed that the existing posts were vulnerable to flooding during the monsoon season.
"Upgrading and relocating the posts to higher ground is an important government initiative to ensure GOF personnel can continue carrying out their duties effectively, including maintaining round-the-clock security surveillance along the border.
"This will also help improve operational efficiency and ensure personnel are better positioned to respond to security requirements," he said.
On security along the East Coast, particularly the Golok River, Suzrin said the GOF's Southeast Brigade deployed three battalions based in Terengganu, Kuantan in Pahang, and Pengkalan Chepa in Kelantan.
He said the battalions operated according to established routines to maintain border security, alongside coordinated enforcement efforts in other parts of the country, including the northern states, Sabah, Sarawak, southern Peninsular Malaysia and maritime areas along the Straits of Malacca.

Title: Foodie Media's net profit soars in first full year as listed firm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Foodie Media Bhd's net profit surged 67.7 per cent to RM15.67 million in its first full financial year as an ACE Market-listed company.
For the financial year ended Aug 31, 2026, Foodie Media's revenue rose 49.6 per cent to RM55.49 million from RM37.09 million a year earlier.
The revenue growth outpaced expansion in the company's digital content, influencer marketing and events business.
For the fourth quarter, its net profit surged more than tenfold to RM4.55 million from RM433,000 a year earlier, while revenue rose 82.5 per cent to a record RM15.82 million from RM8.67 million.
Foodie Media said the quarterly growth was driven by its content, creator and community businesses, supported by stronger demand for sponsored content, key opinion leader (KOL) marketing campaigns and events.
Its content segment recorded a 28.8 per cent increase in full-year revenue to RM30.4 million, while the creator segment grew 59.8 per cent to RM13.6 million.
The community segment was the fastest-growing, with revenue expanding more than sevenfold to RM7.1 million from RM1 million a year earlier, following its inaugural Monie Fest and a fuller events calendar.
Meanwhile, the commerce segment recorded a 10.6 per cent increase in revenue to RM4.4 million.
According to Foodie Media, the combined contribution of its contributing segments rose to 45.3 per cent of total revenue in FY26, from 36.4 per cent previously.
Foodie Media announced a second interim dividend of 0.39 sen per share and a second special dividend of 0.61 sen per share, bringing total dividends for FY26 to 1.53 sen per share, amounting to about RM13.6 million.
Foodie Media chief executive officer Nicholas Lim Pinn Yang said FY26 marked its first full financial year as a listed company, with record revenue and profit supported by growth across all four business pillars.
"Just as importantly, creator, commerce and community now make up close to half of group revenue, which tells us the 4C model is working as intended," he added.
Foodie Media remains positive on its prospects for FY27, supported by the continued shift in advertising expenditure from traditional media to digital and social platforms.
The group said it would continue expanding content production, its KOL network, affiliate commerce and events, while extending its services to new brand clients.

Title: Prabowo's allies turn their backs on troubled free meals scheme
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto's big-tent coalition has given him almost unchecked power for two years, but mass food poisoning and graft linked to his flagship free meals programme have emerged as the first major test of their support for the former special forces commander.
Two political parties in the coalition have already decided, after internal deliberations, to distance themselves from the programme, senior members from both parties with knowledge of the discussions told Reuters. A member of a third coalition party said their party feared the problems with the scheme would hurt their electoral prospects.
Together, the parties of the three people, who asked not to be identified because they feared repercussions for criticising Prabowo's policies, represent more than a quarter of his coalition's 80 per cent parliamentary majority, which includes seven of the eight parties in the house. Prabowo's Gerindra party has 15 per cent.
"Loyalty must also have limits," a member of one of the parties, which was once a vocal defender of the programme, told Reuters.
Prabowo made providing free, nutritious meals a cornerstone of his election campaign, promising to reach 83 million children and pregnant women, but several incidents of mass food poisoning, logistical challenges and allegations of corruption have left many Indonesians questioning the multibillion dollar initiative.
A poll conducted in early October by Saiful Mujani Research and Consulting (SMRC) showed about 62 per cent of the public opposed the programme, while approval for the president himself fell to the lowest since he took office.
"What are the limits? The survival of our party," the party member said, adding internal polls showed the party's electability had fallen in July from January. They did not give further details of the confidential survey meant only for internal party consumption.
"If by mid-2027 there are no improvements, the coalition will be fragile and things may eventually fall apart on their own," they said. Indonesia's next elections are due in early 2029.
Until now, Prabowo — who marks two years in office this week — has faced little or no pushback. There have been no dissenting votes in parliament on any bills the government has proposed, not even by the one party that is not formally part of the ruling bloc. Nor has the leader of Southeast Asia's largest economy faced any speeches critical of his policies.
FALLING NUMBERS
Tensions in Prabowo's coalition have risen as the president's approval rating has declined.
Last November, the president had an 81 per cent rating, according to SMRC. That fell to 66.4 per cent in March, 51 per cent in July and 44.5 per cent in October.
Positive opinions of the free meals programme have also slumped - from 62 per cent last November to just over a third in the most recent poll.
In June, authorities arrested a former chief of the programme and two other officials on corruption charges.
On August 31, dozens of families filed a police complaint against the government, marking the first legal action over the programme that started in January 2025. Early last month, about 1,700 people fell ill in four separate incidents after eating the meals, bringing the total number of cases of food poisoning to at least 57,000 since launch.
The president's office and the National Nutrition Agency (NNA), which runs the initiative, did not respond to requests for comment.
Sugiat Santoso, the Gerindra spokesperson, said the coalition remained strong and the programme was not intended to secure electoral gains.
"Every political party has its own targets and we respect that ... Whatever their stance, related to free meals or not, supporting Prabowo or not, we respect it," Sugiat said, adding that the NNA was working to improve the programme.
The National Mandate Party, one of the six parties in Prabowo's coalition, said it remained committed to supporting the programme. Any shortcomings should be addressed "systematically and collectively," said Viva Yoga Mauladi, its deputy chief.
The other parties did not respond to Reuters requests for comment.
SYMPATHY FOR VICTIMS
A senior member in a second coalition party said an increasing number of voters were complaining about the programme.
The party has asked its lawmakers to start "constructive public criticism" of the scheme using "polite language," the person said.
Both parties where the senior members said they planned to express their concerns publicly, said they also aimed to push the government to improve the programme.
Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka recently publicly apologised for the food poisoning cases, visiting some of the affected children.
Gibran is the son of Joko Widodo, who defeated Prabowo in the 2014 and 2019 presidential elections, and whose backing was key to Prabowo finally winning the presidency in 2024.
Prabowo, meanwhile, has publicly defended the initiative. In February, he played down the food poisoning incidents, saying the number of cases was statistically insignificant.
"99.99 per cent of the programme can be considered successful," he said.
In August, Prabowo pledged improvements.
"I am determined to continue the free nutritious programme but with improvements and efficiency," he said.
'MAJOR BLOW'
The free meals programme has created broader political pressure on coalition parties with ministers from those parties facing criticism and attacks on social media when speaking about it, said Burhanuddin Muhtadi, a senior visiting fellow at Singapore's Yusof Ishak Institute.
If the scheme failed, it would be a "major blow" for the president given it was central to the 2024 election campaign, he added.
"Prabowo could revise his policy by making the programme more targeted, so it would be more feasible to manage and would not incur such high budget. However, it appears he has not significantly changed the universal design, proven by the programme's very large budget allocation next year," Burhanuddin said. The government has budgeted 240 trillion rupiah for the scheme next year.
The problems with the free meals programme are unfolding as the president faces economic challenges from the cost of living to MSCI's warning that it could exclude Indonesia from its stock market indices, potentially cutting it off from international capital.
"Prabowo must demonstrate commitment and integrity, not only making statements," said Mohammad Ezha Fachriza Roshady, SMRC's researcher.--REUTERS

Title: Experts warn Waze location data could expose sensitive movements patterns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government's ban on Waze among civil servants has raised questions about the data security risks posed by navigation applications, with experts saying location data could reveal users' daily routines and movements around sensitive facilities.
Academy of Sciences Malaysia fellow Emeritus Professor Datuk Dr Mohamed Ridza Wahiddin said the decision was technically based on a risk assessment involving the scope of data collected, collection methods, legal jurisdiction and the potential to analyse users' movement patterns.
He said research conducted by Peter Gasper in 2020 had demonstrated that Waze could track users' movements under certain conditions.
"Although this is not evidence of current misuse, it shows that tracking risks have existed from a technical standpoint," he said.
Ridza said allowing Waze to access location data through the "Always" setting could create detailed records of users' daily routines, including their home and workplace locations, frequently travelled routes and visits to sensitive locations.
He added that Waze's "Invisible" feature only concealed a user's location from public view on the map but did not prevent the application from collecting location and route data.
Similar risks existed with Google Maps if features such as Timeline, Web and App Activity, or search service history were enabled, he said.
However, Google states that precise locations transmitted by devices are not stored in search service history or Web and App Activity. Instead, only general areas are recorded, while the associated location metadata is deleted after 30 days.
Meanwhile, cybersecurity expert Aaron Ikram Mokhtar said precautionary measures involving official duties were reasonable, as location data could become sensitive when combined and analysed.
He said the government was concerned that Waze collected location data, travel routes, movement patterns and device information, including when the application was not actively in use.
"If such data is collected from a large number of people, it could reveal movement patterns, including activity around offices or sensitive facilities," he said.
Aaron said legal jurisdiction was another concern, as Waze's terms were believed to specify Israeli law and courts for disputes arising from the use of the application.
"The government is concerned that Malaysia may not have full control over how the data of its citizens and civil servants is processed, accessed or used by parties subject to Israeli jurisdiction," he said.
However, he questioned the decision to single out Waze without a comparable public assessment of Google Maps and other navigation applications, which could also collect location data.
"The measure would be stronger if the government published a detailed risk assessment and applied the same data security policy to all navigation applications, rather than targeting just one," he said.
The government announced the ban yesterday, saying it was intended to protect government information and users' personal data from potential misuse by the Israeli regime.
In a statement, the Prime Minister's Office said the decision took into account Waze Mobile Ltd's status as a data controller incorporated and operating under Israeli law.
It said the Madani government remained firm in its position and would close any avenue that could be exploited by the Israeli regime to threaten national security and the public.
Malaysia is among three countries, alongside Iraq and Iran, that have announced moves to restrict or stop the use of Waze.
Iraq has announced plans to ban the application from 2027, with the possibility of bringing forward implementation to the end of 2026, citing data security concerns and its links to Israel. Iran had earlier blocked and restricted its use.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SUV driver in fatal Penang hit-and-run surrenders to police
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A 23-year-old SUV driver suspected of being involved in a fatal hit-and-run along the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway this morning has surrendered to police.
The crash claimed
the lives of two friends,
a 22-year-old man and a 20-year-old woman from Padang Serai, Kedah, who died at the scene.
Northeast police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said the suspect, from Bukit Jambul, surrendered at the Northeast Police Headquarters around 1pm today.
Rozak said a urine screening test conducted on the suspect returned negative for drugs.
"The SUV driver will be brought for remand tomorrow for further investigation," he said.
He said post-mortem examinations found that the male motorcyclist died from severe head and neck injuries, while his female pillion rider died from severe head injuries.
The crash involved a motorcycle and an unidentified vehicle near the Penang Bridge interchange along the expressway.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 3,435 policemen will be on duty during Melaka election
Article:
MELAKA: There will be 3,435 policemen on duty during the Melaka election.
State police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar said 1,500 of these would come from other states.
He said federal police in Bukit Aman would coordinate the placement of policemen from other states.
Speaking to reporters after a briefing on the 16th state election at the state police headquarters, he said police would have a special team which will use technology to strengthen security throughout the election period.
He said the team would use drones and monitor closed-circuit television cameras especially during nomination and polling days.
Meanwhile, Dzulkhairi said 2,764 policemen will be casting their ballots during early voting on Nov 10, including those voting via post.
The Election Commission has set polling day for Nov 14, with nominations taking place on Oct 31.
In the previous election, Barisan Nasional won 21 of the 28 state seats, while Pakatan Harapan won five and Perikatan Nasional the remaining two.
As of April 20, there were 683,543 registered voters, an increase of 188,348, or 38 per cent, from the 2021 election.

Title: Viral Porsche driver jailed five days, fined RM10,000 for reckless driving
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The driver of a Porsche Cayenne who went viral for reckless driving and taunting other road users has been sentenced to five days in jail, fined RM10,000 and disqualified from driving for five years.
Woo Hong Jiang, 56, an online trader, pleaded guilty in the magistrate's court to reckless and dangerous driving that endangered himself and other road users.
The offence took place at 2.14pm on Oct 18 along the Puchong Highway bypass towards Bukit Jalil, Serdang.
The charge, under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act, carries a maximum jail term of five years and a fine of between RM5,000 and RM10,000.
Magistrate Nur Natasya Mohtaruddin ordered Woo to begin serving his jail sentence immediately. He will face an additional six months in jail if he fails to pay the fine.
The court also ordered that the conviction be endorsed on his driving licence.
Woo was brought to court after his two-day remand expired following his arrest.
Deputy public prosecutor Adriana Maisarah Mohd Farid urged the court to impose a stiff sentence, citing dashcam footage showing Woo allegedly driving recklessly.
"He acts like a road bully. There are dashcam videos showing him driving dangerously and even though no accidents or damages occurred, he had endangered other road users and could have potentially caused a collision," she said.
She argued that a substantial fine and a jail term exceeding the minimum penalty were necessary to deter others from committing similar offences.
"He should be imposed with a high fine and a jail term higher than the minimum as a lesson and deterrent to road users who may think of repeating the same traffic offence," she added.
She also applied for Woo's conviction to be endorsed on his driving licence and for him to be disqualified from driving for five years.
Woo, who was unrepresented, pleaded for leniency.
After the proceedings, he was led out of the courtroom and taken to prison.
Federal Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali confirmed that Woo had paid the RM10,000 fine.
He said Woo was taken to Kajang Prison to serve his sentence.
Hasbullah advised motorists to exercise patience and restraint on the road and avoid reckless or aggressive driving that could endanger others.
"Motorists are also reminded to comply with traffic regulations and refrain from provoking other drivers, as such behaviour could lead to serious accidents and legal action," he said.
A police report was lodged on Oct 19 after several videos of the Porsche Cayenne being driven recklessly went viral on Facebook. The videos were shared on the Dashcam Owners Malaysia page in a post titled "The Infamous Porsche Cayenne in Puchong & Kinrara".
Another motorist lodged a police report the following day.
Hasbullah had earlier said
initial investigations
found that the incident occurred on a three-lane road near Bandar Kinrara 3.
He said the vehicle fitted with the dashcam was travelling from Puchong towards Bukit Jalil in the leftmost lane when the Porsche Cayenne attempted to change lanes without signalling.
The motorist sounded the horn after noticing the Porsche's manoeuvre, prompting its driver to accelerate and give chase, he said.
Hasbullah said the situation escalated when the Porsche driver allegedly braked in an attempt to force the other vehicle to stop.
The Porsche was also seen obstructing the other motorist's path, he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DAPSY wants evidence behind Waze security concerns
Article:
hakimmahari@nst.com.my
KUALA LUMPUR: DAP Socialist Youth (DAPSY) wants the government to review its ban on civil servants on Waze, questioning the lack of publicly available evidence that the navigation application poses a threat to national security.
In a statement today, DAPSY called on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the government to adopt a more pragmatic and transparent approach to cybersecurity concerns.
It said Waze had been widely used by Malaysians for years, but the public had yet to be presented with sufficient evidence that the application had compromised national security or misused users' data.
"While DAPSY acknowledges the importance of strengthening cybersecurity, we question the rationale and justification of officials who proposed this blanket ban.
"Rather than reassuring the public, such a sweeping decision risks generating further questions and undermining public trust," it said.
The youth wing suggested that the government consider targeted safeguards for civil servants handling confidential information or performing sensitive duties, including military personnel, intelligence officers and senior security officials.
It said such measures would address potential security risks without imposing unnecessarily broad restrictions.
It also criticised the government's recommendation to replace Waze with the locally developed TuJu application, citing complaints from users over its technical shortcomings.
"Many users tried TuJu and highlighted technical shortcomings, proving that the application can hardly be a reliable and practical alternative.
"Banning a well-established application in favour of an alternative with significant technical issues risks further eroding public trust in government institutions," it said.
DAPSY urged the government to take public feedback seriously and reconsider the directive before the controversy escalated.
"It is not too late for the government to prevent this issue from becoming a farce," it said.
The youth wing maintained that national security and data protection were important priorities but stressed that decisions affecting the public should be supported by evidence and transparency.
"Safeguarding national security requires sound evidence, transparency and concerted efforts to build public trust."
Yesterday, the government
announced a ban
on the use of Waze among civil servants, citing concerns over the potential misuse of government information and users' personal data by the Israeli regime.
The Prime Minister's Office said the decision took into account Waze Mobile Ltd's status as a data controller incorporated and operating under Israeli law.
The government also encouraged Malaysians to consider the locally developed TuJu application as an alternative for road navigation.
The Malaysian Highway Authority earlier announced that TuJu was undergoing system improvements, temporarily disrupting its navigation function.
Its CCTV viewing feature and other available functions remained accessible.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Palm oil worker jailed nine months for threatening wife with parang
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A palm oil worker who threatened and chased his wife with a parang after accusing her of having an affair was sentenced to nine months' jail by the magistrate's court here today.
Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno imposed the sentence on Ahmad Fairus Mohamed, 42, after he pleaded guilty and after considering the mitigation plea and submissions by the prosecution and defence.
The court ordered the sentence to run from the date of his arrest on Oct 18.
According to the charge, Fairus, who has three children, committed criminal intimidation against his 37-year-old wife using a parang at a house in Senggarang here about 8.30am on Oct 18.
He was charged under Section 506 of the Penal Code, which provides for a jail term of up to seven years, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
According to the case facts, the incident occurred after the complainant, who is also the victim, had an argument with the accused.
The accused then scolded and threatened her before taking a parang from a room and chasing her.
The victim fled to a neighbour's house for help before lodging a police report at the Senggarang police station on the same day, fearing for her safety.
Following the report, police arrested the accused about 1.30pm that day to facilitate investigations.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim prosecuted, while Kamarularifiin Nordin from the National Legal Aid Foundation represented Fairus.

Title: [UPDATED]: Customs seize RM1.33mil in electrical goods, detain warehouse manager
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Customs officers have seized 9,286 electrical appliances worth more than RM1.33 million, including duties and taxes, in a raid on a warehouse in Seri Kembangan, Selangor.
A local man in his 60s, who managed the warehouse, was detained to assist investigations into the suspected smuggling of electrical appliances without the required approvals.
Kuala Lumpur Customs director Wan Norizan Wan Daud said the raid was conducted at a private warehouse in Bukit Belimbing on Oct 13, following intelligence received from the department's headquarters.
"Checks at the premises uncovered 9,286 electrical items of various types and functions believed to be without the necessary Certificates of Approval (CoA) from the Energy Commission and Sirim.
"Those at the premises also failed to produce valid approval documents for the goods during the inspection," she said in a statement.
Wan Norizan said the seized goods were valued at RM1,012,200, while the estimated import duties and taxes amounted to RM323,904, bringing the total seizure value to RM1,336,104.
She said investigations indicated that the electrical appliances were believed to have been smuggled into the country without the required approvals before being supplied to electrical goods distributors.
"The modus operandi involved using local purchase invoices to disguise the origin of the imported goods and avoid detection by the authorities," she said.
Wan Norizan said investigations were ongoing to identify and locate the owner of the seized appliances for further action.
The case is being investigated under Section 135(1)(d) of the Customs Act for storing or possessing uncustomed goods or prohibited imports.
Those convicted face a fine of between 10 and 20 times the customs duty involved, subject to the statutory minimum and maximum calculations, or imprisonment of between six months and five years, or both.
Wan Norizan urged the public to assist Customs in combating smuggling, warning that such offences not only deprived the government of revenue but also threatened national security and public welfare.
She said information on smuggling activities could be channelled to the Customs toll-free hotline at 1-800-88-8855 or the nearest Customs office.
Identities of informants would be kept confidential.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] High Court grants PN stay on RoS deregistration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional has secured a temporary reprieve after the High Court today allowed its application to stay its suspension and subsequent deregistration by the Registrar of Societies (RoS).
The decision comes just nine days before nomination day for the Melaka election, paving the way for the coalition to resume its political activities and preparations to contest under its own name and symbol.
High Court judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad ruled that RoS' decision to cancel PN's registration on Oct 20 did not render the coalition's application for a stay academic.
He said exceptional circumstances warranted granting the stay, particularly the potential harm to PN's political activities and its participation in the upcoming election.
Azizan said certain consequences, including the loss of an opportunity to participate in an election, could not be remedied once they had occurred.
"The court must also consider which party would suffer greater prejudice if the stay was granted or refused.
"Granting the stay would not prejudice the respondents, as PN's political activities could still be monitored by the authorities," he said.
Azizan made the ruling after hearing submissions from lawyer Tan Sri Azhar Azizan Harun, representing PN, and senior federal counsel Nurhaffiza Azizan, representing RoS director-general Datuk Mohd Zulfiqar Ahmad and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
In his decision, Azizan said the main issue raised by the respondents was whether PN's stay application had become academic following RoS' decision to cancel its registration before today's hearing.
The government had argued that the cancellation rendered the stay application ineffective as the administrative action PN sought to prevent had already taken place.
However, Azizan disagreed, saying the court could not determine whether an application had become academic merely because the administrative action being challenged had already occurred.
"The court had to examine the relief sought in its entirety to determine whether there remained a real issue requiring determination."
He acknowledged that a stay order could not automatically restore a registration that had already been cancelled.
However, the judge said the issuance and enforcement of the cancellation notice did not, by themselves, extinguish the purpose of PN's application.
Azizan stressed that his decision did not determine whether RoS' decision to cancel PN's registration was lawful, as that issue would be decided during the substantive judicial review.
The court allowed the stay application pending the full disposal of the judicial review, with no order as to costs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kelantan-Thailand border concertina wire found cut 11 times between March, October
Article:
RANTAU PANJANG: The General Operations Force has recorded 11 cases of concertina wire being cut along the Malaysia-Thailand border in Kelantan between March 27 and Oct 12 this year.
Internal Security and Public Order Department deputy director (GOF) Datuk Mohamad Suzrin Mohamad Rodhi said enforcement action had been taken by the GOF and the respective district police headquarters in connection with the incidents.
He said the incidents were believed to involve deliberate acts aimed at creating entry and exit routes through the border fence to facilitate smuggling activities.
"I believe the parties responsible have been identified based on the information gathered," he told reporters this during a visit to the border here today.
Accompanying him was GOF Southeast Brigade commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain.
Suzrin said GOF would continue to update field intelligence in collaboration with the National Security Council and the relevant police contingents on border intrusions involving the cutting of concertina wire.
He said those on duty would continue repairing cut sections of the wire to restore security control as quickly as possible.
It was learnt that the illegal jetties associated with the cut concertina wire were identified as Abe Li Posmen, Salleh, Kak Mah, Pok Mat, Adam, Abe Yie, Poksu Roni, Syed Agil, Lan Bundle, Cik Ma, Epek, Zin Merah and Gergaji.
It was also learnt that the estimated length of damaged concertina wire at each location is between two and five metres.

Title: Two killed, 8 injured in attack on airport in Saudi oil city Dammam
Article:
DAMMAM:  Two people were killed and eight were injured in an attack on Wednesday evening on King Fahd International Airport in Saudi Arabia's eastern oil city of Dammam, Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation said on Thursday.
Those killed were a Saudi citizen and an Indian national, the authority said. The injuries ranged from minor to serious.
Damage was being assessed, it added.
Airport operations had resumed and air traffic had returned to normal, the authority said.
Earlier, the Saudi energy ministry said that falling debris from the succesful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility killed two people and injured a further two on Wednesday.
"The attempted attack resulted in the deaths of two individuals, a Filipino and a Nepali, and injuries to two others," the ministry said in a statement.
It did not say who launched the drone aimed at Shaybah oil field near the UAE border.

Title: Israeli settlers steal Palestinians' olives as attacks on harvest grow more violent
Article:
BROUGHT to tears as he recalled Israeli settlers hitting his cherished olive trees with sticks and taking off with the olives, Palestinian Ahmed Salem said he feared being attacked if he tried to intervene.
Settlers have intimidated Palestinians harvesting their olives in the occupied West Bank for decades, but this year, not only has violence increased sharply, theft has been widespread, according to Palestinians, Israeli rights groups and the UN.
The settlers dumped Salem's olives into sacks and then drove them to a nearby Israeli settler outpost to be pressed into olive oil, the 50-year-old Palestinian told Reuters of the incident around two weeks ago near his village Lubban al-Gharbi.
"How would you feel if something that belonged to you was being violated, and you could do nothing about it?" he asked.
The couple living in the outpost, whose olive press settlers have urged Israelis to use for West Bank olives, declined multiple Reuters requests for comment, while the Yesha Council, which oversees Israeli settlements in the West Bank, did not immediately respond.
The attacks have accelerated ahead of an Israeli election next week that opinion polls show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his pro-settler coalition could lose to opponents who have taken a more critical stance against settler violence.
The olive harvest starts with the onset of cooler weather, allowing Palestinian families to gather in the lush, terraced groves that they have groomed for generations.
"My six-year-old son remembers going there with me, eating there, making tea there," Salem said.
With the establishment of hundreds of small settler outposts under Netanyahu's government since 2022, the military has increasingly restricted Palestinian access to areas nearby, including many olive groves.
"This creates a situation where Palestinians, in many of the cases, many of the lands, especially in proximity to settlements and outposts, cannot enter the land and harvest the trees," said Ziv Stahl, executive director of Israeli rights group Yesh Din.
"But settlers can come and go freely, and that's what they do."
Even when Palestinians can access their trees, it is not without risk.
[[nid:1561353]]
Yesh Din on Wednesday reported 125 physical attacks on Palestinian olive harvesters over the 24 days since the season began and 168 incidents of crop theft, with Israeli military forces present in at least a quarter of cases.
An Israeli military official said it takes acts of violence, criminal activity and attempts to undermine security very seriously.
The official did not refer to settlers or comment on the reports of olive theft in the presence of the Israeli military, which has separately uprooted trees with excavators, citing what it said was a need to prevent Palestinian attacks.
The removal of Palestinians' olives has met with widely differing responses from Israeli rabbis.
"I call it theft. From my perspective, I define it as theft or robbery, and it is forbidden," said Zev Weitman, the rabbi for the Alon Shvut settlement south of Bethlehem.
Prominent Orthodox rabbi Dov Lior said settlers should harvest across the West Bank, asserting in an open letter that Palestinians had no ownership rights to the land and that harvesting olives fulfilled "the commandment of conquering the land."
Hundreds of acres of the land around Salem's village, Lubban al-Gharbi, including olive groves, were fenced off and seized between 2023 and 2026 by Avichai Farm, an Israeli settler outpost built on a nearby hill.
Salem said villagers have seen settlers harvest olives from the seized land and take them to the outpost's olive press.
At the start of the olive harvest, settlers posted on social media calling on Israelis to harvest West Bank olives and bring them to Avichai Farm's press.
"Both fine oil and strengthening the Jewish hold on the vast expanses of our land!," read a message on a settler Telegram group. "It's either us or our enemy!"
The press at Avichai Farm advertises "premium products produced by Avichai Farm" with olive oil at about US$20 a bottle via a website run by the Farms Association, a settler group that Reuters has reported receives significant financial support from the Israeli government, which says the aim is to promote peace.
The Farms Association did not immediately respond to a request for comment and the couple who live on the farm with their children declined to be interviewed by a Reuters reporter who approached the area on Sunday.
[[nid:1561352]]
On a road leading to Avichai Farm, Reuters spoke to a man who declined to be identified and said he had driven from a settlement around 90 minutes away to press 14 bags of olives from trees he said he grew himself.
Lubban al-Gharbi villagers and other Palestinians who have lost land to settler expansion say the harvesting of olives from trees in groves seized from Palestinian land constitutes theft.
UN bodies and most countries deem Israel's settlements on land occupied in war illegal under international law regarding military occupations. Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied.
During this year's olive harvest, Palestinian authorities say three Palestinians have been killed in daily militant settler attacks, which have also injured several journalists, European diplomats and a French mayor.
Stahl from the Yesh Din Israeli rights group said the violence was "part of a campaign of ethnic cleansing, paving the way for the annexation of the West Bank without its Palestinian population."
Israel, which has considered the idea of annexation, said it is investigating some of the incidents.
An Israeli government spokesperson said olives "picked by a Jew in the ancestral homeland of the Jewish people" did not constitute theft and that Jews owned and cultivated "millions of olive trees" in the area. No one should take the law into their own hands, the spokesperson added.
Palestinian farmer Samer Ben Shamsi said masked settlers attacked him on Oct 9 in the Palestinian village of Beita near Nablus, then sped away in a pickup truck with his harvest of olives after he and other farmers fled.
"This year, they steal without fear because they have a state and a powerful force backing them," Ben Shamsi said, referring to the security forces.
Within the past year alone, settlers had shot him in the leg, beaten him and smashed his possessions, he said.
"We pay in blood for the olives."
* The writers are from Reuters
